Spec:
- `new(capacity)` (capacity >= 1) builds an empty one. ✓ (line 13-15 looks fine)
- `push(buffer, value)` returns the NEW BUFFER (a plain map, never a tuple); when the buffer is full, the OLDEST value is dropped to make room for the new one, so `size/1` never exceeds the capacity.
- `pop(buffer)` returns `{value, buffer}` for the oldest value, or the atom `:empty`. ✓
- `to_list(buffer)` lists the values oldest-first. ✓ (items is stored oldest-first since we append with ++)
- `size(buffer)` is the number of values held. ✓

The bug is in `push`: when the buffer is full, it returns the buffer unchanged instead of dropping the oldest value and adding the new one.

Fix:

```elixir
def push(%{capacity: capacity, items: items} = buffer, value) do
  if length(items) >= capacity do
    [_oldest | rest] = items
    %{buffer | items: rest ++ [value]}
  else
    %{buffer | items: items ++ [value]}
  end
end
```

Since capacity >= 1, when length(items) >= capacity >= 1, items is non-empty, so `[_oldest | rest]` is safe.
